2024:CGHC:5455  
 HIGH COURT OF CHHATTISGARH, BILASPUR  MCRC No. 8742 of 2023  Lokeshwar Singh Thakur S/o Ramnihor Singh Thakur Aged About 29  Years, R/o 762/8, Nawa Anjore Center Street, Devrikhurd Bilaspur, Ps-  Torwa , Tahsil And District- Bilaspur --- Applicant.
 Versus  State Of Chhattisgarh through Police Station- Sarkanda,, District :
 Bilaspur, Chhattisgarh --- Respondent.
(CAUSE TITLE DOWNLOADED FROM CIS PERIPHERY)
For Respondent/State : Mr. Ashutosh Shukla, Panel Lawyer.

This second application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. for grant of bail has been filed by the accused/applicant who has been arrested in connection with Crime No.1009/2022 registered at Police Station Sarkanda, Bilaspur for the offence under Sections 406, 409, 420, 467, 468 & 471 of the IPC.

2. Prosecution case, in short, is that Complainant namely J Ramu Kumar had lodged an FIR on 01.04.2022 stating that he was working as Executive Manager in Medmart Logistic Private Limited Company, which is involved in providing health care equipment to the various hospitals through out the nation.

The Applicant was posted for 4 years at Bilaspur and he committed fraud by selling goods to other co- accused to the tune of Rs.1,04,22,282/- and due to Covid pandemic, audit was not done and when the same was conducted, the said fraud came to the notice of the Company as the material was sent but the Applicant, instead of selling it to Apollo Hospitals, sold it in the open market

, therefore, the offence as aforesaid has been Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:5455 registered Lokeshwar Singh Thakur vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187552208/
1 against him.

sentences.text: It is pertinent to mention here that earlier bail application filed by the applicant was rejected by this Court on 03.07.2023 passed in MCRC No.3156/2023 with liberty to revive his prayer for bail in case the trial is not concluded in next 8 months.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the crime in question.
He further submits that though this Court was directed to expedite the trial but even after lapse of 4 months, not a single witness has been examined.
He has also filed copy of order-sheets of the trial Court in support of his contention.

He also submits that the applicant is languishing in jail since 14.02.2023 and there is no progress in trial, therefore, the applicant may be released on bail.
4.

Per contra, learned State counsel opposes the prayer for bail and submits that earlier bail application was rejected on merits and liberty was granted to the petitioner to revive his prayer for bail in case the trial is not concluded within next 8 months.
Though the said period has not been over but the applicant has preferred the second bail application.
He also submits that huge fraud has been committed by the applicant and co-accused to the tune of Rs.1,04,22,282/-.
Therefore, present is not a fit case for grant of bail.
However, perusal of order-sheets of the trial Court show that on several dates either summons were not issued or the summons which were issued returned unserved by the concerned SHO.
He submits that in every trial Court, an official known as Court Muharrir is posted, who as per direction of the Presiding Officer, issue a summon and submits its report before the concerned Court.
It appears that the concerned Court Muharrir and police officials are not discharging their duties properly.
Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:5455 5.

Having regard to the aforesaid submissions and considering the facts and circumstances of the case; further considering the gravity of offence; that there is no material change in the facts of the case after rejection of earlier bail application; that the liberty was granted to revive the bail application if trial is not concluded within next 8 months, however, said condition is also not fulfilled, I am not inclined to release the applicant on bail.
6. Accordingly, the application is rejected.
7. Before parting, this Court observes that on 03.07.2023 while rejecting earlier bail application the trial Court was directed to expedite the trial.

However, perusal of order-sheets of the trial Court show that on 04.07.2023 accused Lokeshwar was not present before the Court in judicial custody,
therefore, arguments of the parties could not concluded.

Similarly, on 17.07.2023 and 26.07.2023,
the accused could not be produced before the trial Court.

Another order-sheet dated 26.07.2023 shows that accused Lokeshwar was connected before the trial Court from concerned Bilaspur Jail through Video Conferencing and on said date, charges were also framed against him.
The Magistrate has also ordered for issuing summons to prosecution witness No.1 to 3.
Thereafter, the case was listed on 08.08.2023.
However, on the said date also, no summons were issued, therefore, the Court again ordered for issuing the summons.
Thereafter, on 04.09.2023, the summons received unserved and fresh order for issuing summons was passed.

Despite directions of the concerned Presiding Lokeshwar Singh Thakur vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187552208/
2 Officer, this practice continued on several dates till 15.01.2024 and not a single witness has been examined.

sentences.text: Prosecution Officer was also present on the date of hearings but no steps were taken by him.

Even, the summons ought to have been issued the Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:5455 Court Muharrir and if summons were not returned, the said fact should have been informed to the Superior Police Officer.
Learned Magistrate has neither taken any steps in this regard nor initiate any action against erring official.
8. In these circumstances, it is expected from the concerned Superintendent of Police to conduct preliminary enquiry after examining the facts.
On enquiry, if any negligence is found on the part of the concerned official, then suitable steps may be taken against him.

The concerned District Judge shall also call a report from the concerned Presiding Officer as to why summons were not issued despite the order and if the Court Muharrir or the concerned official who is entrusted to issue summons is found to be negligent, then what steps has been taken in this regard.
If the said action has not yet been taken, suitable steps be taken against concerned erring officer(s) in accordance with rules.

9. The concerned Court is further directed to proceed with the trial expeditiously in compliance of order dated 03.07.2023 and in the spirit of Section 309 of the Cr.P.C.
10.
Learned State counsel and Registrar (Judicial) shall send copy of this order to the concerned Authorities for necessary information and compliance.

Sd/-
